jp: 朝[あさ]早[はや]く目[め]{が|ga-subject}覚[さ]める{ように|youni-purpose}、夜[よる]{は|wa-topic}早[はや]く寝[ね]ます。
en: I go to bed early at night so that I wake up early in the morning.
why: 覚める is not something you control, so the goal is joined with ように, not ために.

jp: 花[はな]{が|ga-subject}きれいに咲[さ]く{ように|youni-purpose}、毎日[まいにち]水[みず]{を|o-object}やっています。
en: I water the flowers every day so that they will bloom beautifully.
why: The flowers' blooming is outside the speaker's control, so the goal takes ように.

jp: 速[はや]く泳[およ]げる{ように|youni-purpose}、毎日[まいにち]プール{で|de-place}練習[れんしゅう]しています。
en: I practise at the pool every day so that I can swim fast.
why: The potential form 泳げる states a hoped-for ability, which is joined to the action with ように.

jp: 山[やま]{で|de-place}寒[さむ]くない{ように|youni-purpose}、あたたかい服[ふく]{を|o-object}持[も]って行[い]きます。
en: I'll take warm clothes so that I won't be cold in the mountains.
why: Not being cold is a state, not an act of will, so the purpose is expressed with ように.

jp: ぐっすり眠[ねむ]れる{ように|youni-purpose}、夜[よる]{は|wa-topic}コーヒー{を/は|o-object}飲[の]みません。
en: I don't drink coffee at night so that I can sleep soundly.
why: 眠れる is a potential state you hope for, so the purpose is joined with ように.
